vulnerability.title: Symfony UrlGenerator anchors a raw alternation requirement incorrectly, so a middle alternative can match a substring and yield a protocol-relative off-site URL

vulnerability.category_l2: an ungrouped alternation in a route requirement lets a substring match a middle alternative, so an attacker-influenced route parameter such as _locale can be set to //host and produce a protocol-relative off-site URL

critical_operation.description: doGenerate() builds the requirement validation pattern as "#^" . $token[2] . "$#i" where $token[2] is the raw route requirement. For a requirement written as an alternation such as "en|fr|vi|de", the ^ and $ anchors apply only to the first and last alternatives, so any middle alternative matches anywhere in the supplied value. A value like "/evil.com" therefore passes because it contains "vi", and the same value is then substituted into the generated path, which begins "//evil.com/" and is interpreted by browsers as a protocol-relative URL to another host. The 5.4.52 fix wraps the requirement in "(?: ... )" so the anchors cover the whole alternation. The host-token branch at line 247 had the same defect and is fixed in the same commit.

entry_point.description: An application route declares a requirement as an alternation (a locale list is the common case) and passes a request-influenced parameter to the Twig path()/url() helpers or to UrlGenerator::generate(). The requirement check is the gate that is bypassed.

trace.description: generate() resolves the route and calls doGenerate() with the user-supplied parameters
doGenerate() checks each variable token against the anchored raw requirement; with an alternation a middle alternative matches as a substring
the accepted value is substituted into the path as $token[1].$mergedParams[$varName].$url, so "/evil.com" yields a path beginning "//evil.com/..." that browsers treat as protocol-relative

source_crosscheck.notes: NVD, the CNA, GHSA/OSV and symfony.com agree on the mechanism, CWE-185/CWE-601, the <5.4.52 range and the v5.4.52 release. The GHSA names the 5.4 fix commit and the advisory resolution matches the diff. NVD has both a Primary CVSS 3.1 6.1 MEDIUM metric (nvd@nist.gov) and a Secondary CVSS 4.0 2.3 LOW metric (the CNA vector); the GHSA MODERATE label tracks the 3.1 score. The canonical severity keeps the CNA 4.0 vector, and both scores are recorded in all_published_scores.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read UrlGenerator::doGenerate at v5.4.45 and confirm the requirement is interpolated between ^ and $ without grouping.
An independent reviewer must confirm bcf487c2 is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.52, and that the fixed pattern adds the non-capturing group.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 and the fixed release is 5.4.52.
An independent reviewer must assess whether an attacker-controlled route parameter is necessary for reachability and record that prerequisite.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No PHP runtime, Symfony application or route was executed; the finding is static.

Reachability requires application code to pass a request-influenced value into a route parameter whose requirement is an alternation; the advisory describes the pattern but no specific application was tested.
The browser interpretation of a leading // as protocol-relative is standard behavior but was not exercised here.
Only the 5.4 branch was fetched and compared; 6.4.40, 7.4.12 and 8.0.12 were not diffed.
NVD carries no primary CVSS metric; the 2.3 LOW score is the CNA vector republished as Secondary. GHSA labels it MODERATE, which disagrees with the 2.3 Low base score.

NVD publishes two metrics for this CVE: a Primary CVSS 3.1 6.1 MEDIUM from nvd@nist.gov and a Secondary CVSS 4.0 2.3 LOW from the CNA. The canonical severity keeps the CNA 4.0 vector; the GHSA MODERATE label is consistent with the 3.1 score, not with 2.3.
open_questions: How many upstream route defaults use alternations that contain short substrings was not surveyed.
Whether the host-token branch (line 247) is independently reachable with user input was not traced through application call sites.
